Compute Match — Product
Overview
What is Compute Match?
Compute Match, also called the
Compute MatchMake
System
(internal project key
NCPMS
, code name
Clustruffle
), is an NVIDIA web platform that connects
customers
who need GPU compute capacity with
NVIDIA Cloud Providers (NCPs)
who own and operate GPU
infrastructure.
In one sentence: customers find GPU clusters, send reservation
requests, and NCPs accept, negotiate, and contract those requests, while
NVIDIA Platform Admins oversee the marketplace.
Who uses Compute Match?
There are three personas:
Persona
Who they are
What they do
Customer
(also called
Offtaker
or
requester)
An organization that needs GPU compute
Browse available GPU clusters, submit reservation requests (to one
or several NCPs), submit custom requests, track and cancel requests
NCP
(NVIDIA Cloud Provider / GPU Compute
Provider)
An organization that operates GPU data centers
Upload GPU capacity via CSV, review incoming reservation requests,
accept, reject, counteroffer, and confirm contracts
Platform Admin
(NVIDIA operations / business
admins)
NVIDIA staff running the marketplace
Explore global capacity, review future capacity uploads, onboard
NCPs, approve NCP access requests, broker custom requests, extend
deadlines, view analytics dashboards
A single user can hold both customer and NCP access; they switch
between them with
Switch profile to
in the account
menu.
The core idea in five steps
NCPs publish capacity.
An NCP uploads a CSV
describing how many GPUs of which platform (for example H100, B200,
GB200) are available, in which country and city, and from which
date.
Customers search.
A customer opens
Find a
Cluster to Reserve
, filters by platform, region, country, GPU
count, tenure, and earliest start date, and sees matching clusters on a
world map and as cards.
Customers request.
The customer submits a
reservation request
for one cluster, or for up to 3
clusters from different NCPs at once (multi-NCP request). If nothing
fits, they submit a
custom request
that NVIDIA admins
broker manually.
NCPs respond.
Each selected NCP receives an email
with a secure
magic link
. The NCP accepts (moving the
request to
In Process
), rejects, or counteroffers, and
finally clicks
Confirm Contract
.
Contract.
The first NCP to contract wins; the other
NCPs’ offerings on the same request are cancelled as superseded.
Capacity is allocated, and the deal is synced to Salesforce as an
Offtake record.
Key business objects
Object
Meaning
GPU Offering / GPU Capacity
A cluster an NCP makes available: GPU platform, hosting provider,
region, country, city, GPU count and availability date windows
Capacity type
AVAILABLE
(current capacity, starts within 90 days of
upload, published right away) or
FUTURE
(starts more than
90 days out, needs Platform Admin review)
Reservation Request
A customer’s request to reserve GPU capacity
Reservation Request Offering
One NCP’s slice of a reservation request; a multi-NCP request has
one per NCP, each with its own status and deadlines
Proposal
One version of the reservation terms (dates, GPU count, platform,
region, price). The customer’s original request is the first proposal;
NCP counteroffers add more
Custom Request
A request without a specific cluster; NVIDIA admins move it through
Open, In Review, Matched or Unserviceable
Allocation
Capacity consumed once a request is contracted
Import Job
One CSV capacity upload and its processing status
Access Request
A pending request from a partner (for example via the NPN portal) to
join as an NCP
Important timers (defaults)
An NCP has
7 days
to accept a request routed to
them (acceptance window).
After accepting, the NCP and customer have
45 days
to reach a contract (contract negotiation window).
Reminder emails are sent
3 days
before each
deadline.
A magic link is valid for
1 hour
, and can be
regenerated for up to
7 days
after routing.
Custom requests never expire automatically.
Platform Admins can extend either window by
1 to 200
days
.
Technology at a glance
Frontend:
Next.js 15, React 19, Ant Design 6,
Tailwind CSS 4, NextAuth 5 with Keycloak.
Backend:
Python 3.13, FastAPI, Domain-Driven Design
with hexagonal architecture, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, Alembic
migrations.
Workflows:
Temporal (Temporal Cloud in shared
environments) with a Python workflow worker.
Identity:
Keycloak with NVIDIA Starfleet SSO,
custom Keycloak extensions.
Analytics:
Apache Superset dashboards.
Platform:
Google Cloud — GKE Autopilot, Cloud SQL
PostgreSQL, Memorystore Redis, Secret Manager; deployed with Terraform
and Helm through GitLab CI.
Integrations:
Salesforce (Offtake sync and
partner-domain sync), email notifications.

Match — Signing Up, Signing In and First-Time Setup
How sign-in works
Compute Match uses
Starfleet
, NVIDIA’s single
sign-on service, through
Keycloak
. Sign up and Login
use the same flow.
Open the home page and click
Get Started
,
Sign up
or
Login
.
On the
/login
page enter your
Work
email
and click
Login
.
Personal email domains (Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail and similar) are
blocked with an explanation. Use your work or enterprise email.
You are redirected to Starfleet and your organization’s identity
provider (for example NVIDIA corporate login or your company SSO).
After authentication you return to Compute Match. You may briefly
pass through several authentication pages; this is normal.
Technically, the frontend uses NextAuth 5 with the Keycloak client
customer-web
in the
customer
realm, and passes
kc_idp_hint=starfleet
to send users to the Starfleet
identity broker.

user (

).

(

you will get an email when activated.

(

your access request. Once approved, the page shows

NCP sign-in paths
Welcome email
New NCP users created by NCP onboarding receive a
provider_welcome
email with a direct login link.
Magic link (respond to a
reservation)
When a reservation request is routed to an NCP, users in that NCP
organization who have the
provider_business_user
role and
belong to the
offering-validator
group get an email with a
magic link.
The link is a Keycloak action token created by the custom
accept-reservation-token
extension.
Keycloak validates the token and a one-time nonce with the backend
(
POST /api/v1/offering/validate-nonce
), blocks the link if
a different user is already logged in, creates a session and
redirects.
The browser lands on
/automatic-login?from=magic-link&callbackUrl=...
, which
skips the email page and reuses the SSO session, then opens
Manage reservation
so the NCP can
Accept
.
A magic link is valid for 1 hour. NCPs or admins can resend one
(
POST /api/v1/provider/offering/{offeringId}/resend-magic-link
)
within 7 days of routing.
NPN portal
NVIDIA Partner Network (NPN) members can reach Compute Match directly
from the NPN portal (feature flag
NPN_PORTAL_INTEGRATION_ENABLED
). They still pass through
the work-email page and Starfleet. If their partner organization is not
onboarded yet, an access request with source
NPN_PORTAL
is
created and they wait on the access-pending page.
How partner detection works
Compute Match keeps a
partner domain
mirror of
email domains belonging to NVIDIA partners, synced from Salesforce twice
a day.
Domain lookup statuses are
PARTNER
,
NOT_PARTNER
and
PENDING
.
Personal mail providers can never be partner domains.
When a user from a partner domain signs up and their NCP is not
onboarded,
POST /api/v1/user
creates an
access
request
(statuses
PENDING
,
APPROVED
,
REJECTED
; sources
NPN_PORTAL
,
SIGNUP
).
A Platform Admin approves or rejects it under
Onboard NCPs →
Review Onboarding Requests
. Approval provisions the
organization and user in Keycloak; rejection emails the reason. A
rejected applicant can apply again, which creates a new request.
Signing out
Use
Logout
in the account menu. If your session
cannot be refreshed, the app shows a recovery screen and performs a full
Keycloak logout.

Frequently asked questions
How do I sign up?
Click Sign up or Login, enter your
work email, and sign in through Starfleet. Personal emails are not
allowed.
Why do I see “Access denied”?
Your identity was
verified but your account is not authorized under current policies.
Contact computematchmake@nvidia.com or sign in with another work
account.
Why do I see “Your access is being reviewed”?
Your
company is an NVIDIA partner but its NCP organization is not on the
platform yet. A Platform Admin must approve your access request.
How many NCPs can I send one request to?
Up to 3 in
the UI by default (backend allows up to 10), if you have the multi-NCP
permission.
Will I get several contracts if I send to several
NCPs?
No. The options are alternatives; the first NCP to
confirm the contract wins and the others are cancelled.
How long does an NCP have to respond?
7 days to
accept, then 45 days to contract. Reminders arrive 3 days before each
deadline. Admins can extend both.
My magic link says it expired.
Links last 1 hour.
Ask for a resend (possible for 7 days after routing) or log in normally
and open Manage reservation.
Can I accept an NCP counteroffer as a customer?
The
customer detail page is view and cancel only; the NCP confirms the
contract after you agree with them directly.
When can I cancel?
While the request is Awaiting NCP
Acceptance, awaiting approval, In Process or Expired; custom requests
while Open or In Review.
What if no cluster matches my needs?
Submit a custom
request. Admins will review and mark it Matched or Unserviceable.
My CSV upload shows Pending Review.
It contains
future capacity (starting more than 90 days out); a Platform Admin must
accept it.
My CSV upload shows Validation Failed.
Open “See all
details” for row errors. Check the five required columns, UTF-8
encoding, 10 MB and 10,000-row limits.
Why can’t I see Upload Capacities or Manage
reservation?
You lack the scope (
manage_inventory
or
approver_manage_reservation_request
). Basic NCP users
are read-only. Ask your Platform Admin.
I have customer and NCP access. How do I switch?
Use

at the top of the account menu.
Where is the user manual?
Click the book icon in the
header; it opens the manual filtered to your role. The

icon shows help for the current page.
What does What’s New show?
Release highlights for
your persona. A banner appears on your landing page for about 7 days;
dismissing it keeps it under the bell icon. Use
Mark All as
Read
to clear the unread dot.

Use

in the header, or answer the star rating after
creating a request or uploading capacity.
